merge.title: Capped, reboot-surviving inter-attempt PIN back-off inside gated_unlock (Trezor parity, closes #637) plus an S-SRAM cooldown on host-initiated unlock prompts that the user dismissed
merge.threat: Two distinct, both bounded. (1) Physical attacker with intermittent access (evil-maid) who harvests wrong-PIN unlock traces or runs glitch sweeps on the PIN gate: today the only brake is the 10-attempt count; there is no delay scaled by the failure count anywhere on the unlock path. The attempt rate is NOT USB speed in production: the PIN can only be supplied through the secure-world 2-button dialog (8 positions, 500 ms long-press per position, so roughly 4-5 s per attempt minimum even with electrically actuated buttons) and there is no NS path that carries a PIN outside e2e-test. (2) Hostile companion while the device is LOCKED: every INS 0x10 pops the trusted PIN dialog unconditionally and arms a fresh 120 s window; after Cancel or idle expiry the host can re-issue immediately, so the host controls when and how often a PIN prompt is on the glass (nag / habituation / scheduling PIN entry for a capture). No attempt is burned unless a human submits a PIN, and the device is locked with no secret loaded, so this is a nuisance and conditioning vector, not a key-extraction path.
merge.proposal:
ONE firmware change in two parts, both S-world only, no wire-format, flash-layout or hardware change.

Part A (core, parity): in `nsc::gated_unlock` (secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1394), after the double-read of page 124 yields `pre_count` and BEFORE `pin_attempts_bump`, block for `min(2^pre_count - 1, CAP)` seconds measured on the secure SysTick tick (`timeout::now()`), with a trusted-UI countdown and left-button cancel that returns before the precharge (cancel = no attempt consumed, mirrors Trezor UNLOCK_UI_CANCELLED). Placing it in gated_unlock covers all three callers at once (cmd_request_unlock.rs:100, boot unlock loop main.rs ~4175, PendSV re-unlock main.rs:4567). Because the delay is recomputed from the persistent page-124 count on every call, a power cycle does not shorten it. CAP must be chosen below the existing watchdog/idle envelope: recommended CAP = 60 s (schedule 0,1,3,7,15,31,60,60,60,60 = 297 s for the full 10 attempts instead of Trezor's uncapped 2^n-1, which would put a 511 s wait on attempt 10). The wait must hold a `timeout::TrustedUiWaitGuard`-equivalent and refresh activity (device is LOCKED, so this does not extend a signing session), otherwise the shipping IWDG `MAX_BUSY_TICKS = 30_000` compute deadline fires. Read the delay input through the same double-read/sentinel discipline as the gate so a single fault on the load cannot zero it; skipping the delay must never skip the precharge (keep it a separate `#[inline(never)]` call ahead of the existing FAIL-IN bump gate). Compile out under `e2e-test` / bench modes exactly as `sign_rate` does (sign_rate.rs:147,166). Put the pure schedule function in a workspace crate (not `secure/src/nsc`, which is excluded from host tests) with a host test and a Kani bound. Then update docs/security/HARDENING.md:280 (currently under '5.3 Consider') and docs/security/threat-model.md:431 ('eventual progressive delay', and the false 'button entry without echo') to match what ships; close #637.

Part B (optional, small, beyond parity): in `cmd_request_unlock::run`, keep an S-SRAM counter of consecutive host-initiated prompts that ended in `Cancelled` or `IdleWipe` and a not-before tick; while inside the cooldown (1,2,4.. capped 60 s) return an existing status without painting the display. Reset on any successful unlock. Use an existing NscStatus (UserRejected=6) rather than adding a new `Cooldown` variant so the proto/USB status-word mapping and companions are untouched. S-SRAM only, no new flash state.

If the owner declines Part A, the minimum deliverable is the doc correction alone (move the HARDENING/threat-model lines to explicit residuals), which is what #637 asks for.

members.note: Core back-off kept (2^fails-1 s from page-124 pre_count, before the precharge, S-only tick, countdown, left-button cancel, doc fix for #637). Added a 60 s cap and the IWDG/idle-guard requirement that the proposal missed. Dropped: 'finish the countdown' as a timing-equalisation claim, and the 'USB speed' and 'independent of CMD_GET_REMAINING' framings (see dropped_parts). Priority lowered from P1 to P3.

Same mechanism as pin-06; merged. Its 'apply the same wait before the PendSV retry' is satisfied for free by placing the delay inside gated_unlock. Its #692 motivation (persistent SE fault burning the budget quickly) is already handled by PENDSV_MAX_NO_VERDICT_FAILURES = 3 (main.rs:4466), so that justification is dropped. 'Costs nothing' is wrong: it needs the watchdog guard and a cap.

The asserted behaviour is confirmed in code (locked INS 0x10 pops the dialog unconditionally, no rate bound). Kept only the S-SRAM cooldown, narrowed to prompts the user dismissed or ignored and to an existing status code. Dropped the 'press to unlock' gesture screen, the new NscStatus::Cooldown, and the PendSV gesture gate.

dropped_parts: pin-06 'attacker can drive attempts at USB speed': refuted. Production `enter_pin` (secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs:54-140) is the only PIN source; the constant-PIN arm exists only under e2e-test (pin_entry.rs:172-175), which nsc/mod.rs fences out of production. Minimum per-attempt time is about 8 x LONG_PRESS_MS (500 ms, hw/buttons.rs:183) plus the dual-SE verify.

pin-06 'run the remainder of a pre-computed total so wrong and right paths take the same announced time' as a side-channel fix: dropped. The PIN compare is in SE silicon; `DualSe::unlock` calls SE050 even when OPTIGA rejects (dual_se.rs:370-377), so wrong-PIN latency carries no per-digit information, and the verdict is displayed anyway. Trezor's 'Finish the countdown' (storage.c:1233-1240) is UI progress completion, not a timing countermeasure. Real-vs-duress latency is already op-count matched (nsc/mod.rs:1503-1512).

pin-06 'make the back-off independent of the attempt log and CMD_GET_REMAINING so it cannot be probed': dropped as incoherent. The attempt count is already disclosed to NS by CMD 1 and the attempt-log INS, and the delay is a deterministic function of that count; there is nothing to hide.

Uncapped 2^fails-1 schedule: infeasible as written on pq1. Attempt 10 would block 511 s inside a handler; the shipping IWDG stops kicking after MAX_BUSY_TICKS = 30,000 ticks (hw/iwdg.rs:137) unless a TrustedUiWaitGuard is held AND the 120 s idle deadline has not expired (hw/iwdg.rs:29-31, timeout.rs:27). Replaced by a 60 s cap with an explicit guard.
SCA-08 #692 justification: already implemented differently. Verdictless failures are bounded at 3 before the loop abandons with the budget intact (main.rs:4452-4473, 4609-4622).

USB-07 'press to unlock' passive screen before the keypad: dropped. It adds a press to every unlock but the user who is being conditioned presses it and types the PIN anyway; the PIN is typed on the trusted display so the host gains nothing from the prompt itself, and no attempt is consumed without a physical submit. Also adds a new screen to the ui-px image that is already 76,949 B over the secure slot.
USB-07 new `NscStatus::Cooldown`: dropped. Adds a proto enum value, a USB status-word mapping and companion work for a nuisance-class issue; an existing status suffices.

USB-07 gesture gate on the PendSV idle re-unlock loop: dropped. That prompt is device-initiated by the idle timer, not host-schedulable, and is already bounded at 12 passes (main.rs:4448, 4521); the starvation concerns are tracked under #692/#700/#175.
USB-07 'blocks NS/USB for 120 s' as a harm: true mechanically but the starved party is the hostile host itself; not a security argument.
tracked_issues: #637 (OPEN, priority:low): progressive inter-attempt PIN delay is a HARDENING proposal, not implemented; deliverable = implement or move to residual. This is Part A in full.
#148 (CLOSED): F3 REQUEST_UNLOCK idempotency; fixed only for the already-UNLOCKED state (cmd_request_unlock.rs:21-31). The LOCKED-state prompt rate (Part B) is outside its scope.
#692 (OPEN): PendSV runaway guard / SE-fault budget burn on e2e images; adjacent, partially mitigated by the verdictless cap; a back-off in gated_unlock slows it further but does not close it.

#715 (OPEN) and #119 (OPEN): attempts consumed with no user error / wedge burns page 124 to self-wipe; a back-off turns a fast fault-driven walk to the wipe into a slow one, giving the user time to power off. Side benefit only.
#700 (OPEN): trusted-UI flows never exercised on pq1 silicon; any countdown UI inherits this validation gap.
#600 (OPEN): signing-ceremony anomaly layer; sign path only, does not cover unlock prompts.
#713 / #728 (CLOSED): reset_activity on the locked path; Part B must not regress these (arm the window only when the prompt is actually shown).
merge.untracked_delta: (1) The concrete design constraints for #637 that the issue does not state: cap below the IWDG busy deadline and 120 s idle window, placement inside gated_unlock before the precharge so all three callers and reboots are covered, FI discipline on the delay input, e2e/bench bypass, and a host-testable schedule function. (2) The LOCKED-state host-prompt storm: no issue tracks that a locked device shows a PIN prompt on every unsolicited INS 0x10 with no rate bound and that a dismissed prompt can be re-raised instantly. (3) threat-model.md:431 still claims 'button entry without echo', which #637's own text says is false; the fix is named in the issue body but not as a deliverable.
decision_conflicts: No recorded decision forbids this. The work-todo argument against a global random-delay-interrupt timer (archive ~line 1962) concerns jitter inside crypto, not a deterministic human-scale wait before the PIN gate; no conflict.

Invariant 'NS does not control the inactivity timer': the back-off wait must refresh activity only while LOCKED, following the #713/#728 precedent (cmd_request_unlock.rs:45-52, main.rs ~4150-4161). Refreshing while unlocked would violate HIGH-13 / X17-UI3.
'No new per-signature flash state' / invariant #8: respected. Part A reads the existing page-124 count; Part B is S-SRAM only.

PIN-dialog content rule recorded at main.rs:4533-4548 (the NN/12 counter was removed because varying diagnostic text on the PIN screen habituates users): a countdown is varying text on the same trusted-path screen. It needs a fixed, designed screen separate from the PIN row, and an owner UX sign-off.
ui-px flash budget: the ui-px image is 76,949 B over the secure slot; a new px countdown screen adds to an open owner decision. The legacy 16x4 path has 34,071 B headroom and can use `show_status`.

Trezor-parity sweep 2026-07-20 and the 2026-06 critical-port memo do not list PIN back-off as ported or declined (grep for backoff/progressive in both returns nothing), so this is neither a re-raise nor a reversal.
prerequisites: Owner decision on #637: implement (Part A) or reclassify as a residual. Doc correction is required either way.
Owner UX decision on the cap value and on a countdown screen that is visually distinct from the PIN row.

A blocking tick-based wait helper in secure world that holds the trusted-UI wait guard; today only calibrated busy-loop `delay_ms` copies exist per driver (hw/buttons.rs:195, ui/lcd.rs:314) and the SysTick `timeout::now()` tick. SysTick must be able to preempt the caller: true for NSC handlers and, since #729, for PendSV; verify for the boot unlock loop.
Schedule function in a workspace crate with host tests, because `secure/src/nsc` and `secure/src/hw` are cfg(not(test)).
Silicon validation needs a pq1 unit with a panel and a non-e2e image (#700); the bench pq1 board has no LCD and e2e-test compiles the path out.
merge.precedent: Trezor ships Part A: storage/storage.c:1158-1161 `get_backoff_time_ms` = 1000*((1<<fail_ctr)-1); :1199-1207 sleeps before the fail-counter increase with `ui_progress()` cancel returning UNLOCK_UI_CANCELLED; :1314 folds the back-off into the announced total; :1233-1240 finishes the UI countdown on a wrong PIN. Trezor's delay is uncapped with PIN_MAX_TRIES attempts. Ledger enforces a small attempt count with wipe and no documented exponential delay (not verified in source here). Part B has no vendor precedent: Trezor's `_pinlock_filter` (core/src/apps/common/lock_manager.py:261-268) raises the unlock dialog on any non-allowlisted host message while locked, with no rate bound.
merge.rationale: Verified absence: no delay scaled by failure count exists on any unlock path. The only delays are `fi::wait_random()` jitter (about 0-19 us per the comment at nsc/mod.rs:1405-1407) at cmd_request_unlock.rs:92 and nsc/mod.rs:1414/1430/1502, and `sign_rate::MIN_SIGN_INTERVAL_MS = 1000`, which applies to signing only. grep for backoff/cooldown/progressive across secure/src, shared/src, nonsecure/src returns nothing PIN-related. Why P3 and not the members' P1/P2: (a) the attempt count is capped at 10 by page 124 and SE050 silicon, with E120 as a 32-lifetime backstop, so the back-off multiplies the cost of at most 9 traces per user-unlock cycle (about 45 s becomes about 5 min with a 60 s cap); (b) attempts are already human-paced by the button dialog; (c) the back-off is keyed on the same page-124 count as the lockout, so the counter-reset or rollback primitive the members cite as the motivating threat resets the delay too. It adds nothing against that attacker, exactly as on Trezor. Its real value is making glitch/SCA campaigns on the gate slower per sample and making the HARDENING/threat-model text true. Part B is nuisance-class. Cost S for code, but the countdown screen and silicon validation depend on #700.

merge.residual_after: An attacker who can reset or roll back page 124 also resets the back-off (same state); the directional E120 > page-124 boot wipe and the SE050 silicon counter remain the real defence there. A glitch that skips the delay call still meets the unchanged precharge and sentinel gates, so the delay is no FI barrier in itself. The 10-attempt bound still permits up to 9 wrong-PIN traces per user-unlock cycle, now over about 5 minutes instead of under one. A shoulder-surfer still sees the live digit, and the countdown length reveals the failure count (already readable over USB). A hostile host can still raise one PIN prompt per cooldown period (at most one a minute at the cap) and still fully controls prompt timing on the first request; with the gesture gate dropped, the keypad itself still appears on host request. S-SRAM cooldown state is lost on power cycle, which the host cannot cause but a physical attacker can. Nothing here is validated on pq1 silicon with a panel until #700 closes. The advisor review and the Codex MCP second opinion were both unavailable this run, so this reconciliation is single-reviewer.

skeptic.reason:
The core survives: no failure-scaled delay exists on any unlock path, #637 is open and asks for exactly "implement or reclassify", Trezor ships the mechanism (storage/storage.c:1158-1161, 1199-1207), and no recorded decision forbids it. Both listed live defects are confirmed in source. P3 is the right ceiling.

The recommendation is wrong in one place that blocks Part A as specified. It treats the watchdog envelope as something the new wait must fit under, but by my source read (not built or run with `iwdg` on) the existing PIN dialog already does not fit under it.

**Axis 1, bypass and residual**
- Part A adds almost nothing against the stated attacker. Attempts are human-paced and capped at 10, so it stretches at most 9 attempts per victim-unlock cycle from about 45 s to about 5 min.
- The SCA motive is weaker than stated. The MCU-side secrets on this path (SCP03 and PBS session keys) are exercised at every session setup with no attempt cost, so a back-off does not ration those traces. The PIN compare is in SE silicon.
- A glitch campaign on the gate already pays one page-124 precharge per shot (secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1476-1493). The delay only slows 10 shots.
- Anyone who can reset page 124 resets the delay too; the merged text says this.
- Net value is honest docs and parity, not a new barrier.

**Axis 2, feasibility**
- No board, flash-layout or FSBL change. Boot cost is zero when the failure count is zero.
- The watchdog facts differ from the recommendation; see corrections 1 and 2.
- The boot unlock loop is safe for a tick-based wait: SysTick starts early on hardware (secure/src/main.rs:1643-1644) and `hw::iwdg::init()` runs only after the loop (main.rs:4257).

**Axis 3, tracking**
- The tracked list is accurate; I re-checked the state of each.
- Missing: #802 (SysTick TRNG draw every ms after 120 s idle, which shares the tick the wait would use), #329 (owner prompt-abuse semantics, forced-blind only, adjacent to Part B) and #729 (closed; the PendSV priority fix Part A depends on).
- No issue tracks the locked-state prompt storm or the watchdog/PIN-dialog interaction.

**Axis 4, decisions**
- No conflict found. Grep for back-off, progressive and exponential in trezor-comparison.md, the 2026-07-20 parity sweep, STATUS.md and the 2026-06 critical-port memo returns nothing PIN-related.
- The work-todo argument against a random-delay-interrupt timer is about jitter inside crypto and does not apply.
- The PIN-screen content rule (main.rs:4533-4548) does bind the countdown screen, as the merge notes.
skeptic.corrections:
1. **Watchdog premise is wrong; guarding the PIN dialog is a hard prerequisite for Part A.**
- `TrustedUiWaitGuard` is taken only at secure/src/ui/confirm.rs:194 and secure/src/ui/px/lcd.rs:750.
- `enter_pin` (secure/src/ui/pin_entry.rs:99-145) and `buttons::wait_event` (secure/src/hw/buttons.rs:300) never take it.
- `reset_activity` touches only `LAST_ACTIVITY`; nothing resets `BUSY_TICKS` or `STALL_TICKS` on a button press. The only writers are in secure/src/hw/iwdg.rs.
- So the shipping PIN dialog already runs against the watchdog budgets before any back-off starts. Part A must first put the guard around PIN entry, then around the back-off wait.

2. **The PendSV path is bound by the 4 s stall limit, not the 30 s busy limit the recommendation cites.**
- PendSV (secure/src/main.rs:4490-4628) holds no `HandlerGuard`, and the NS heartbeat is bumped only in the NS poll loop (nonsecure/src/main.rs:231-236).
- That selects the stall branch: `NS_STALL_LIMIT_TICKS = 4000` (iwdg.rs:126), then about 2 s of hardware timeout.
- The USB path (cmd_request_unlock.rs:35) does hold `HandlerGuard`, so it gets `MAX_BUSY_TICKS = 30_000` counted from veneer entry.

3. **Drop "refresh activity during the wait".**
- The submit long-press already calls `reset_activity` (pin_entry.rs:112) immediately before `gated_unlock`, and a 60 s cap is under the 120 s timeout.
- A refresh also cuts against the test-pinned rule that entering a wait never refreshes inactivity (secure/src/secure_fi_pin_rng_pure_tests.rs:1695-1698).
- Only the guard is needed.

4. **Cancel needs a new `UnlockError` variant.**
- `PinLocked` triggers `trigger_lockout_wipe` (cmd_request_unlock.rs:159-163).
- `InternalError` and the PendSV catch-all `Err(_)` increment `no_verdict`, so three cancels would show "SE fault / power cycle" (main.rs:4609-4622).
- A new variant touches the `secure_element` error enum, three caller matches, `pin_attempt_log` and the source-text tests in main_sau_pure_tests.rs.

5. **Placement alternative the merge did not weigh.**
- Inside `gated_unlock` the wait runs after PIN submit, so the user's PIN sits on the S-stack for up to 60 s. This matches Trezor.
- A shared helper called before `enter_pin` at the three sites gives the same rate limit without holding the PIN, at the cost of three call sites.
- This is an owner or implementer choice, not a defect.

6. **Boot-loop prerequisite can be closed.**
- "Verify SysTick can preempt the boot unlock loop" is settled: SysTick starts at main.rs:1643-1644 on `stm32u585`, and the IWDG is not started until main.rs:4257.
- QEMU starts SysTick late (main.rs:4250), so a tick-based wait must be `stm32u585`-gated or it hangs there.

7. **Part B should be dropped or filed as an issue only.**
- It does not bound the threat it names. An ignored prompt stays up for 120 s and can be re-raised, so with a 60 s cap the PIN prompt is still on the glass about two-thirds of the time, and the first host-scheduled prompt is untouched.
- Returning `UserRejected` with nothing painted tells the companion the user cancelled when the user did nothing.
- A legitimate user who dismissed by mistake gets up to 60 s of silent refusal.
- The #148 idempotency fix is trivially sidestepped: the host sends INS_V2_LOCK (nonsecure/src/usb/commands.rs:287, 504) and then INS_V2_UNLOCK. The locked-and-USB-alive state is therefore host-reachable at will, not only after idle expiry.

8. **Threat (1) wording.** Remove "harvests wrong-PIN unlock traces" as a motive, for the reason given under axis 1. State the value as doc truth plus parity plus a slower walk to the wipe under #715/#119.

9. **Minor.**
- #637's body cites HARDENING.md:170; the text is at :280.
- Add #802, #329 and #729 to the tracked list.
- The "Ledger" precedent line is unverified and should be removed or labelled as such.
- Fact (g) holds for the bump itself (mod.rs:1476), but an ordinary wrong PIN still advances E120 and the SE050 UserID through `se.unlock`. No change needed.

10. **Cost is M, not S.**
- An edit to the FI-critical `gated_unlock`, which has source-text tests.
- The new error variant.
- The guard prerequisite.
- A workspace-crate schedule function with a Kani census re-lock.
- A fixed countdown screen needing owner UX sign-off.
- Silicon validation blocked on #700, with `iwdg` off in every bench image.

Test-pinned rule that entering a trusted-UI wait never refreshes inactivity (secure/src/secure_fi_pin_rng_pure_tests.rs:1695-1698): the merged 'refresh activity during the wait' conflicts with its spirit and is unnecessary with a 60 s cap. Drop it.

The TrustedUiWaitGuard doc contract (secure/src/timeout.rs:194-199) scopes the guard to waiting for a physical button. A countdown that polls only for cancel stretches that contract, so the doc and the pure tests in main_sau_pure_tests.rs:1571-1583 need a deliberate update.
PIN-dialog content rule (secure/src/main.rs:4533-4548): varying text on the PIN screen was removed on purpose. The countdown must be a separate fixed screen with owner UX sign-off.
ui-px flash budget: the image is already 76,949 B over the secure slot, so a px countdown screen adds to an open owner decision. The legacy path can use show_status.

Part B returning UserRejected for a prompt that was never shown changes the meaning of an existing status word that companions rely on. Dropping the new enum value avoids a proto change but creates a semantic one.
